# LC-OFF — replication package

[REDACTED]
[REDACTED]

Source code and raw measurements for:

> **LC-OFF: A Lightweight, Type-Aware Task Offloading Framework for Heterogeneous
> Edge Workloads — with a Capacity-Predictable Admission Threshold at Scale**
> Ming-Chiao Chen, National Taitung University
> Submitted to *Simulation Modelling Practice and Theory*.

**Teaching companion:** [joechen0420.github.io/lc-off](https://joechen0420.github.io/lc-off/)
— a bilingual walkthrough of the decision rule, an interactive calculator for the
admission threshold, and the three points where this research produced
reasonable-looking numbers that were wrong.

The state described in the paper is archived at
[10.5281/zenodo.21648597](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21648597), tagged
`v1.0-submission`. Cite that DOI for the exact snapshot the paper reports;
[10.5281/zenodo.21648596](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21648596) always
resolves to the latest version. This repository keeps moving — a later commit
is not what the paper measured.

Everything reported in the paper is produced by the code here. The per-run
metrics behind every median are included, so a reported number can be traced to
the run it came from without re-executing anything.

---

## What is here

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `lc-off-core/` | The placement engine: gate, weighted multi-criteria scoring, DAG-monotonic reduction, capacity models, overflow policy. Pure Java, no simulator dependency. 37 unit tests. |
| `lc-off-sim/src/` | The iFogSim2 harness: topology builder, planner, per-device module namespaces, the per-request latency recorder, the planning-cost benchmark. |
| `lc-off-sim/*.ps1` | Sweep scripts, one per experiment set (see below). |
| `lc-off-sim/lib/` | ojAlgo, used by the ILP reference bound. |
| `data/` | Raw per-run metrics: placement summary, network usage, both averaging conventions, latency percentiles and deadline attainment, for every run behind the paper's tables. |
| `tools/make_figures.py` | Regenerates the paper's figures. Every number is transcribed in the script with the note it came from. |

**The manuscript is not included here.**

## What is not here, and why

**iFogSim2 is not vendored.** The harness extends it without modifying it, so
you supply your own copy and can confirm that no simulator internals were
changed:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Cloudslab/iFogSim.git vendor/iFogSim2
cd vendor/iFogSim2 && git checkout 5f68d3947e450d8d2b4af42670be819206be68c9
```

That is the exact commit the reported results were produced against. iFogSim2
is MIT-licensed; see its own `LICENSE.txt`.

Every extension in `lc-off-sim/src/` is a subclass or a separate class.
`RecordingActuator` extends `Actuator`, `SeededSelectivity` implements
`SelectivityModel`, and the placement logic plugs in through `ModulePlacement`.
No file under `vendor/` is edited, which is what makes an independent check of
these results possible.

## Requirements

- JDK 17 or later (results were produced with Temurin 21)
- PowerShell 5.1 (the sweep scripts) — the Java itself is platform-independent
- Python 3.10+ with `matplotlib` and `numpy`, only for `tools/make_figures.py`

## Reproducing the results

Compile the core, then run a sweep. Each script compiles the harness itself.

```powershell
cd lc-off-sim
./perdevicesweep.ps1 arvr C 5     # per-fog admission threshold, 20 devices
./perdevicesweep.ps1 arvr E 3     # k* against fog capacity (1400/2800/5600)
./perdevicesweep.ps1 arvr F 3     # non-uniform per-fog thresholds
./perdevicesweep.ps1 arvr G 1     # deadline attainment on a fine grid
./perdevicesweep.ps1 arvr H 3     # k* across topology shapes
./perdevicesweep.ps1 arvr I 2     # does cloud latency move k*?
./perdevicesweep.ps1 arvr J 2     # does a congestible cloud path move k*?
```

Runtime at 20 devices is about 7 s per run. **50-device runs take 30–58 minutes
each and need `-Xmx20g`**: under per-device module identity the cloud host
carries 3N module VMs, and iFogSim updates every VM on that host on every event.

The end-to-end decision cost measurement does not run a simulation at all, so it
scales to fleets the simulator could not:

```powershell
java -cp <classpath> tw.lcoff.sim.PlanCostBench arvr "500,1000,2000,4000"
java -Dlcoff.tierLookup=linear -cp <classpath> tw.lcoff.sim.PlanCostBench arvr "500,1000,2000,4000"
```

## Configuration flags

All default to the behaviour used for the main results, so an unflagged run
reproduces the baseline.

| Flag | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `-Dlcoff.capacity` | `static` | Capacity model: `static`, `reactive`, `fairshare` |
| `-Dlcoff.overflow` | `999999` | Per-fog admission threshold *k* (default: disabled) |
| `-Dlcoff.overflowPerFog` | — | Per-fog thresholds, comma separated, indexed by gateway |
| `-Dlcoff.fogMips` | `2800` | Fog node capacity |
| `-Dlcoff.cloudLatency` | `100` | proxy→cloud uplink latency, ms |
| `-Dlcoff.cloudBw` | `10000` | proxy→cloud uplink bandwidth |
| `-Dlcoff.deadlines` | `50…500` | Deadline grid for attainment reporting |
| `-Dlcoff.seed` | — | Seeds tuple selectivity, making a run bit-reproducible |
| `-Dlcoff.tierLookup` | `hash` | `linear` restores the pre-optimization scan, for the decision-cost comparison |

## On reproducibility

Tuple selectivity is probabilistic, so runs differ by 0.5–1% at identical
settings. **Every figure in the paper is a median over independent runs with the
spread stated**, which characterizes that variability rather than hiding it.
`-Dlcoff.seed` makes a single run bit-reproducible for exact checking; it is off
by default so the reported medians come from genuinely independent runs.

Each run prints `RNG seed=N` or `RNG unseeded`, so a log states its own
provenance.

## Reading the data

`data/*/set*-metrics.txt` holds, for every run: the placement summary (how many
modules landed on fog, cloud and device), total network usage, both averaging
conventions with sample counts, latency percentiles, and deadline attainment
counted per request and per device.

An `INVALID` line in a run means the harness's own assertions failed — a module
was not created, or the latency recorder disagreed with the simulator's
bookkeeping — and that run's numbers are not usable. **No run behind the paper
carries one.**
